tasks.title: Visible go-to-latest chevron: away-only visibility + goToRealtime click (D57.1)
tasks.description: Add the glyph-only chevron <button> to chart_assets/lwc/chart.html (hidden by default, keyboard-focusable with aria-label, absolute-positioned bottom-right of the price axis) and drive it from chart_assets/lwc/chart.js: a new chevronVisible() returning !isFollowing() (visible whenever the viewport is away, with or without new bars; hidden while following), superseding affordanceVisible's away-AND-new-bars rule for the visible control per S-P18-1 (newBarsSinceAway bookkeeping stays internal, still probe-observable); click wiring calls the unchanged goToRealtime(); visibility toggles on the existing viewport-change notification path only (no polling). followLive, fitAndFollow, fitToWidth and the follow derivation itself are untouched. Repro-first: the away-without-new-bars visible cell is the red proof against the old rule.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Given a main-chart viewport either away from the newest bar or following it, with or without newly arrived bars, when the visibility rule is queried, then the chevron is visible if and only if the viewport is away — visible in every away cell including away-without-new-bars, hidden in every following cell. This supersedes P11's affordanceVisible away-AND-new-bars rule (recorded, not silent).

AC2: Given the chevron visible while away, when it is clicked, then the existing goToRealtime scroll-to-edge action runs unchanged — span preserved, newest bar at the edge, follow re-engaged, badge consumed — and the chevron hides by derivation.

AC3: Given any viewport state, then the chevron renders as a glyph with no text label at the bottom-right of the price axis, is keyboard-focusable with an aria-label, is hidden by default, and is toggled only on the viewport-change notification path (no polling), visible only while away per AC1.

tasks.title: Fresh per-timeframe framing with follow-state memory (D57.2)
tasks.description: Compute the fresh-frame Python-side in ui/lwc_view.py (LwcChartView): per load for a different symbol and per set_timeframe change, derive a cutoff — intraday session-anchored via market_calendar mode-aware windows (1 min to start of 2 sessions back; 5 mins 5; 15 mins 10; 30 mins ~22; 1 hour ~44; 4 hours ~126) or daily+ calendar-anchored (1 day minus 1Y, 1 week minus 1Y, 1 month minus 5Y off the newest-bar ts) — clamp the cutoff to the oldest loaded bar, map first-ts->=cutoff to _logical slots mirroring the page's newest-window padding convention, and emit the {range, following} frame post-set_series through the existing range-op wire shape (zero bars is a no-op via the existing empty-series path). Q95 (b) precedence with lineage: set_symbol to a different symbol and any set_timeframe change always request a fresh frame — the Q75 remembered range is never restored (retiring S-P11-5's range leg, follow-state leg stands); remembered following still applies (following or default-true for no memory frames the live edge; remembered-away back-shifts minimally so the newest slot falls outside the range and away derives honestly). Same-symbol data replaces (backfill waves, mode switches) keep S-P11-3 preserve behaviour; TIMEFRAME_CONFIG durations and session_windows are read-only. chart.js gains only the frame-application branch applying an explicit fresh frame over the preserved-range path (ordered after the rows, deferred via the existing needsFit retry when unlaid-out). Y-framing is library autoscale, assertion-only (S-P18-5, A163).
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Given a fresh load for a different ticker with loaded bars on each of the nine timeframes, when the series lands, then the initial visible x-range equals the AC-D57.4 span for that timeframe (1 min last 2 sessions; 5 mins last 1 week; 15 mins last 2 weeks; 30 mins last 1 month; 1 hour last 2 months; 4 hours last 6 months; 1 day last 1 year; 1 week last 1 year; 1 month last 5 years).

AC2: Given loaded bars narrower than the AC-D57.4 span, when the frame applies, then the cutoff clamps to the oldest loaded bar so the frame covers what is loaded with no fetch change; given a zero-bar load, then the frame is a no-op through the existing empty-series path with no error.

AC3: Given a switch back to a previously-seen symbol or a timeframe change on the same symbol, when its bars land, then a fresh per-AC1 frame applies and the Q75 remembered range is not restored; the remembered following still applies — following (or no memory) frames the live edge with tracking, remembered-away back-shifts minimally with following==false deriving honestly and maximal recency — while same-symbol data replaces (backfill continuations, mode switches) still preserve the viewport per S-P11-3.
AC4: Given framed bars exist, then the visible price range covers the framed bars' low-to-high (library autoscale over the framed window); no explicit y-range op is emitted.

tests.description: Parametrized offscreen seeded-series frame cases, one per timeframe (nine cells: session-anchored intraday cutoffs and calendar-anchored daily+ cutoffs), asserting the emitted initial logical range matches the AC-D57.4 span.
tests.expected_result: All nine timeframe cells frame to their spans; session anchoring holds across holidays and RTH/ETH switches via the calendar.

tests.description: Offscreen clamp case (loaded bars narrower than the span: frame covers the oldest loaded bar, no extra request issued) and zero-bar case (no crash, empty-series path, no frame op).
tests.expected_result: Clamped frame covers all loaded bars with zero fetch change; zero-bar load is a silent no-op.

tests.description: Offscreen switch-back case: symbol A (following) to B and back to A asserts a fresh AC1 frame on A (remembered range not restored) ending at the live edge with tracking; covers Q95 (b) overriding the Q75 range memory with lineage.
tests.expected_result: Fresh frame on switch-back; remembered following honoured; no range-restore op emitted.

tests.description: Offscreen timeframe-change freshness plus remembered-away encoding: change timeframe on the same symbol asserts a fresh frame (no viewport preserve), and a remembered-away fresh frame asserts following==false with the newest slot outside the range and maximal recency (minimal back-shift).
tests.expected_result: Timeframe change re-frames fresh; remembered-away frame derives away honestly without burying recent action.

tests.description: Offscreen same-symbol replace cases (backfill continuation wave, RTH/ETH mode switch) asserting the viewport is preserved per S-P11-3 — Q95 covers loads and timeframe changes only.
tests.expected_result: Same-symbol replaces preserve; D51.2 no-yank path intact.

tests.description: Offscreen y-coverage cases over the framed window asserting the visible price range covers the framed bars' low-to-high whenever bars exist.
tests.expected_result: Visible price range covers framed bars; no explicit y op asserted (library autoscale).

Depends on P18-T1 (chevronVisible) and P18-T2 (fresh-frame directive) — verifies their joint behaviour only, edits no production files. Test files only.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Given a fresh frame applied under each follow state, then while following the chevron is hidden, while remembered-away the chevron is visible; a chevron click after a fresh frame lands the span-preserved live edge with follow re-engaged; Fit/reset after framing leaves chevron state consistent via the existing fitAndFollow path.

AC2: Given the P11 suite pinning the superseded badge rule, then its away-alone-hidden assertions are rewritten to away-only (visible) with the supersession recorded as declared churn; no protected assertion is weakened or deleted.
